title: Forward fontSize, fontFamily and opacity on decoration attachments
body:
# Forward `fontSize`, `fontFamily` and `opacity` on decoration attachments

The editor's renderer already applies `fontSize`, `fontFamily` and `opacity` to a decoration's
`before`/`after` attachment, and the internal render-options interface already declares all
three — but `ThemableDecorationAttachmentRenderOptions.from()` builds an explicit allowlist that
predates that support, so an extension's values are dropped on the way out of the extension host
and never reach the renderer.

This adds the three properties to the converter and to the public API. No renderer change is
needed; the plumbing on the other side of the boundary is already there.

## Evidence, at `main` (518720d5)

The renderer collects them for attachments:

- `src/vs/editor/browser/services/abstractCodeEditorService.ts:801`
  ```ts
  this.collectCSSText(opts, ['verticalAlign', 'fontStyle', 'fontWeight', 'fontSize', 'fontFamily',
      'textDecoration', 'color', 'opacity', 'backgroundColor', 'margin', 'padding'], cssTextArr);
  ```
- `src/vs/editor/browser/services/abstractCodeEditorService.ts:587,604-605` — `_CSS_MAP` has
  `opacity: 'opacity:{0};'`, `fontSize: 'font-size:{0};'`, `fontFamily: 'font-family:{0};'`.
- `src/vs/editor/common/editorCommon.ts` — `IContentDecorationRenderOptions` declares
  `fontSize?: string`, `fontFamily?: string`, `opacity?: string`.

The converter drops them:

- `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTypeConverters.ts:508-527` —
  `ThemableDecorationAttachmentRenderOptions.from()` returns a literal with twelve keys; these
  three are not among them.
- `src/vscode-dts/vscode.d.ts:1119` — the public interface omits them for the same reason.

## Before / after, from an extension's point of view

```ts
const type = vscode.window.createTextEditorDecorationType({
    before: {
        contentText: '[2, 8, 128]',
        width: '14ch',
        color: new vscode.ThemeColor('editorInfo.foreground'),
        fontSize: '10px'          // ← not in the API before this change
    }
});

editor.setDecorations(type, [new vscode.Range(0, 0, 0, 0)]);
```

**Before:** the attachment renders at the editor's font size. `fontSize` is not accepted by the
public type at all, and a cast past it is silently dropped by the converter.

**After:** the attachment renders at 10px, because the value now reaches the renderer that
already knew what to do with it.

There is a workaround today, and it is the reason this is worth fixing: `fontStyle` *is*
forwarded and is interpolated into the generated CSS unchanged, so `fontStyle: 'normal;font-size:10px'`
injects the declaration. That works, and it is the kind of thing that stops working without
warning. A one-line allowlist addition is a better answer than a hole.

## Motivation

Gutter-style annotations — a fixed-width column of shapes, sizes or timings rendered left of the
code via `before` attachments — read better at a smaller size than the code they annotate, the
way line numbers do. Inlay hints are not an alternative here: they take no width, so they cannot
hold a column, and they take their colour from six global theme keys rather than per-hint.

The shipped precedent for this kind of readout is decorations: `extensions/git/src/blame.ts`
uses an `after` attachment with a `ThemeColor` and per-range `renderOptions`.

## Tests

`src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/extHostTypeConverter.test.ts` gains one case asserting the
converted object, following the snapshot-style `assert.deepStrictEqual` the surrounding suite
uses.

```
./scripts/test.sh --grep ExtHostTypeConverter
```

## Notes

- No behaviour changes for existing extensions: three optional properties are added, and an
  extension that sets none of them converts to exactly what it converted to before.
- `opacity` and `fontFamily` are included because the renderer collects them in the same call as
  `fontSize`; adding only one of the three would leave the same asymmetry for its two immediate
  neighbours.

title: Share one model-selection policy between Workbench chat and the Agents Window
body:
Workbench chat and the Agents Window both had to answer "which model does this chat open on?", and they answered it differently. The Agents Window had its own engine for it, `transitionModelSelection`, which lived in shared code but had exactly one caller — so it bought nothing, and the two windows were free to disagree.

They did. If a chat had a model restored onto it, the Agents Window treated that as the user's choice and left it alone, while Workbench treated it as leftover from the previous chat and let `chat.defaultModel` overwrite it.

## What changed

**One implementation, and the second is deleted.** The Agents Window now uses Workbench's `ChatInputModelSelectionController` through the existing runtime seam. `SessionModelSelection` is the adapter that connects them. `transitionModelSelection` and its supporting types are gone.

**Chats say where their model came from.** `IChat.modelSource` records whether a model is the chat's own (`Chosen`) or was put there for it (`CarriedOver`), and `setModel` makes the caller say which. Only a chat's own model outranks `chat.defaultModel`, and the model id alone cannot tell you which case you have.

It is required rather than optional, because an absent value has to mean something: it is read as the chat's own, since the alternative is overwriting a model the user picked. A provider that cannot account for a model says `undefined` deliberately.

**Model state is per chat.** Everything about a chat's model is keyed by chat resource, so one chat's choice can't leak into another.

## Behaviour changes

Five, all deliberate — worth knowing if you bisect here:

- A model a new peer chat only inherited no longer blocks `chat.defaultModel` from seeding it.
- "Is this conversation empty?" is read from the chat, not the session, so a new peer chat in a finished session can still be seeded.
- A resumed agent-host session restores its model from the saved draft. Needed because a chat that has already run is never given a model, so without this a reopened session would show one but not actually have one.
- `forkChat` inherits the source chat's model and agent, matching `createSideChat`, instead of taking the session default.
- A chat waiting for a model its pool hasn't published keeps waiting, even after you visit another chat and come back. Previously the temporary stand-in could be mistaken for the chat's real answer, and the awaited model was lost.

## Testing

Both windows run the same conformance matrix (`modelSelectionConformance.ts`). Each case checks both what the picker shows and what the chat actually runs on. Every field is read through `conformanceInputs`, whose fields are all required, so if one side stops reading a field it fails to compile instead of quietly testing something else. That guard caught a real gap: the Workbench side had been ignoring `catalogResolved`.

The matrix covers precedence once the model catalog has settled. It is not a parity proof: while models are still loading the two windows differ. The Agents Window waits — blank picker, send blocked — rather than pick a model it might have to change. Workbench chat shows a stand-in and lets you send, then swaps in the real model when it publishes.

That difference is worth being honest about, because it is not free. Both windows write the selected model to the same place (the chat draft, which is what a resumed session reads back), so a stand-in is visible to the backend either way. If you send in the window before the real model arrives, Workbench sends on the stand-in; the Agents Window won't let you. The rule that actually matters is shared — a stand-in never replaces the model a chat is waiting for — but the send gating is not, and aligning it is a follow-up: making Workbench wait would block the composer on every cold start, which needs its own change and its own justification.

### Verification

- Full `vs/sessions` suite — 2380 passing
- Full `vs/workbench/contrib/chat` suite — 5957 passing
- Component fixtures — 1072 rendered, 0 errors
- `valid-layers-check`, `tsc --noEmit -p src`, eslint — clean

Layering is unchanged: `vs/sessions` imports from `vs/workbench`, never the reverse.

title: chat: describe BYOK Responses failures that omit error details
body:
## Summary

- BYOK chat requests that fail mid-stream now explain what happened instead of showing `{"code":0,"message":"","metadata":{}}`.
- Failures carry the provider's response id, so a user report can be correlated with the provider's own logs.
- A stream error that arrives without a message no longer replaces the reason the request already computed.
- Restores diagnosability for these failures; it does not change when or why a provider fails.

Related to #330408

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

The OpenAI Responses contract requires `code` and `message` whenever a terminal event carries a non-null `error`. Providers violate this in practice and terminate a stream with an error object that is present but field-less.

`mapResponsesApiError` only guarded against a null or absent error. A present-but-empty object fell through: `message` collapsed to `''`, and `metadata.code` became `undefined`, which `JSON.stringify` drops. The result was an error struct with no information in it.

BYOK amplifies this. `hydrateBYOKErrorMessages` promotes the serialized stream error to the entire user-facing reason, so the hollow struct became the whole message. An upstream outage, a malformed request, and a transport fault were indistinguishable, which is why earlier reports of this string were triaged as generic request failures.

### Implementation

`mapResponsesApiError` now separates a usable error from a non-conforming one. When no message is present it synthesizes a description naming the terminal event, the response status, and the response id; the wording adapts depending on whether a provider code survived. Metadata keys are spread conditionally so serialization can no longer reduce them to `{}`.

Callers supply that identity through a small context helper, applied at all three call sites that share this mapping (`error`, `response.incomplete`, `response.failed`), so the invariant is restored once rather than patched per branch.

`hydrateBYOKErrorMessages` gained a matching guard: it keeps the fetcher's original reason when a stream error carries no message, which prevents any future producer of an empty error from blanking the message again.

### Behavior and constraints

- Well-formed errors are unchanged; their provider message and code still pass through.
- Successful responses are unaffected. OpenAI sends `error: null` on success, which continues to map to `undefined`.
- Synthesized text contains only the event type, status, response id, and provider code. No prompt content or credentials.
- `metadata` gains a `responseId` key when the response envelope supplies one, including for well-formed errors.
- Chat Completions is untouched; it forwards the provider error verbatim and never produced this shape.

### Review context

The mapping dates to 1.121.0 and is byte-identical through 1.133.0, so the broken serialization is not a recent regression. What changed is exposure: the Agent Host BYOK proxy moved from Chat Completions to Responses in 1.132.0, which first routed Agents Window traffic through this path eight days before the first report. The editor-window BYOK path has advertised the Responses endpoint for much longer, which matches an earlier report of the identical string on 1.130.0.

The reference to #330408 is deliberately non-closing. Repeated live requests against the affected model, including agent-sized payloads and a counterfactual that toggled the request fields VS Code sends only to that model family, all completed normally. The request shape is therefore not a deterministic trigger, and the underlying failure is unexplained. A transport-layer hypothesis remains open: an earlier report of this same string was resolved by switching the fetcher, and the reports here span both local and remote hosts, where the available fetcher differs. Once this ships, the surfaced message should identify which of those paths is responsible.

</details>

## What changed

- use active-turn chat file edits for the provider-owned Last Turn Changes changeset while a turn is running

- route the live changes pill to the same moving changeset

The changes pill observes file edits directly from live chat output, while Last Turn Changes previously waited for the host changeset diff. title: "Copilot CLI" can still show when session migration is enabled

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
- I enabled the migration setting
- I clicked a Copilot CLI session
- It opened as a "Copilot CLI" session, not an agent host session
- After a bit, it migrated and I had to click it again to reopen it

This was a little confusing because it meant that after the mgiration kicked in, the open session did not actually appear in the list.

I have a lot of SDK sessions, and the initial listSessions pass is extremely slow because of this. Is the EH session provider still active when the migration setting is enabled? Or, did it only show up because of the local view-level session cache?

---

## What went wrong

This is a startup/discovery race, not a setting propagation problem.

- `migrateLegacyCopilotCliEnabled` reached Agent Host as `true` at **10:45:48.953**.
- Agent Host began scanning **4,158 Copilot SDK sessions**.
- You opened `copilotcli:/6b3dccdb-…` at **10:46:01.258**, so the extension-host provider rendered it.
- Agent Host did not finish classifying the catalog until **10:46:12.821**, when it discovered 209 adoptable legacy sessions.
- The Agent Host version of this specific session was announced at **10:46:12.849**, about 11.6 seconds after you opened the legacy version.
- The UI was still rendering the legacy `copilotcli:` session at **10:46:32.179**.

### The underlying code problem

`getSessions()` only hides a legacy `copilotcli:` entry after an `agent-host-copilotcli:` entry with the same raw ID already exists. Before Agent Host discovery finishes, the legacy row remains visible and clickable.

When clicked, `_showSession()` resolves the exact `copilotcli:` resource, so it opens through the extension-host provider. When the Agent Host twin arrives later, the list is deduplicated, but the already-open session is not redirected or replaced.

The long delay comes from `_discoverCopilotChats()`, which classifies the entire SDK catalog before emitting any discovered sessions.

## Important detail

The bundle does **not** show this session actually migrating during the captured interval:

- There is no `Adopting legacy session 6b3dccdb-…` entry.
- There is no Agent Host subscription/restore for that session.
- It was still opened as `copilotcli:` after its Agent Host twin had been announced.

What looked like eventual migration was probably the list refreshing and selecting/opening the newly discovered Agent Host entry, rather than the original open being correctly redirected.

## Expected fix

The invariant should be enforced before discovery completes:

1. With migration enabled, do not surface openable extension-host `copilotcli:` rows that are eligible for Agent Host migration.
2. Explicit opens of legacy URIs—recent history, restored state, or links—should resolve through a migration-aware Agent Host open path rather than directly opening the legacy provider.
3. Incremental or faster discovery would improve the delay, but it would only mitigate the race; it would not fix the correctness issue by itself.

No source changes were made during this investigation.

title: Agent Host: background client auto-cancels side chat ask_user requests after 5s grace window

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

body:
A background window that has an agent session open — but does **not** have that session's side chat open — auto-cancels the side chat's `ask_user` (chat input) requests after the 5s unobserved grace window. The cancellation is reported back to the model as an empty answer, so the agent sees blank responses and concludes the question UI is broken.

## Repro

1. Open an agent-host session (Copilot CLI provider) in window A.
2. Open the *same* session in window B, then leave B idle (do not open the side chat there).
3. In window A, create a side chat on that session and ask the agent to run an interactive Q&A (any flow that calls `ask_user`).
4. Answer the question in window A.

**Expected:** the answer reaches the agent.
**Actual:** ~5s after each question appears, it is cancelled. The tool result delivered to the model is `User responded: ` (empty). The agent retries and eventually gives up with something like "the question responses are arriving blank."

## Evidence

From an Agent Host debug log export (session `copilotcli:/7b1237b7…`, same day, same session):

| Chat | `ask_user` calls | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| default chat | 35 | all answered normally |
| side chat `ed341250…` | 4 | **all blank** |

Every side-chat request was cancelled at almost exactly 5.00s after being raised:

```
08:22:27.480  [Copilot] User input request: requestId=26399d8f…
08:22:32.485  [AgentService] dispatchAction: type=chat/inputCompleted,
              clientId=d8c2cb9c-dfc1-42ad-b48e-14043bb4e304, clientSeq=11
              {"requestId":"26399d8f…","response":"cancel"}
08:22:32.486  [Copilot] User input response: response=cancel
→ chat/toolCallComplete result content: "User responded: "
```

Identical for the other three requests (clientSeq 12, 13, 14).

Key detail: the cancelling client `d8c2cb9c…` is **not** the window that rendered the question. The rendering window (connection `910c1d14…`) was correctly subscribed to the side-chat channel and rendered the carousel (`kind: questionCarousel`, `ChatListItemRenderer#renderQuestionCarousel`). The cancelling client's only other activity was a draft change in the session's *default* chat 11 hours earlier — it woke up solely to emit these four cancels.

## Cause

`_watchForSessionInputNeeded` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts` runs in **every** client that has the session open. It is driven by the session-level `inputNeeded` queue, which by design contains blockers from *all* chats in the session, including side chats.

The `SessionInputRequestKind.ChatInput` branch (~line 2273) cancels after `UNOBSERVED_CLIENT_TOOL_GRACE_MS` (5000ms) unless the request was claimed:

```ts
if (cancelled || this._renderedRequests.get().has(inputKey)) { return; }
```

`_renderedRequests` is an **in-process observable, local to each window**. So "did anyone claim this?" actually means "did *I* claim this?". A background client cannot know another window is rendering the carousel, and its cancel wins the race.

The default chat is immune because every client with the session open renders it and therefore claims it. A side chat only exists as a chat editor in the window that created it, so a background client never claims it.

Note the sibling `ToolClientExecution` branch *does* have an ownership guard:

```ts
if (initial.clientId !== this._config.connection.clientId) {
    return; // A different client owns this call.
}
```

The `ChatInput` branch has no equivalent.

Introduced in 180ee1eb594 ("agentHost: drive tool execution from the session input queue", #328989).

The `ToolAuthentication` (~line 2408) and confirmation-deny (~line 2427) branches use the same window-local `_renderedRequests` check, so side-chat MCP auth flows and tool confirmations are likely auto-cancelled/auto-denied the same way.

## Secondary issue

An `ask_user` cancellation surfaces to the model as `User responded: ` — an empty answer rather than an explicit cancellation signal. That is why the agent kept retrying (four times) instead of stopping: it had no way to distinguish "user submitted nothing" from "your request was cancelled". Cancellations should be distinguishable in the tool result.

## Workaround

Close the other window that has the session open, or open the side chat in that window too.

## What changed

- use active-turn chat file edits for the provider-owned Last Turn Changes changeset while a turn is running

title: fix localization format string parsing
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331074

## Root cause

The About dialog was showing the commit SHA in the `OS:` field because the NLS formatter only parsed the first character of a placeholder index. In `src/vs/nls.ts`, the code used `rest[0]` when replacing `{10}` / `{11}` entries, so `{10}` was treated as argument index `1` instead of `10`.

This was latent for years, but it became visible when the Copilot package versions were added to the About dialog in #329027. That change introduced double-digit placeholders (`{8}` to `{10}`), causing the value for the `OS:` line to resolve to the commit SHA instead of the OS string.

This is a broader NLS bug as well: any localized string with placeholders above 9 would be mis-substituted.

## Fix

Parse the full captured digit group (`parseInt(rest, 10)`) when resolving placeholder indexes, rather than only the first character. This fix is applied in both the main NLS formatter and the vendored Copilot copy.

Also adds a regression test covering multi-digit placeholders.

title: Consider bringing back local model dictation for non copilot users

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
> **Dictation (speech-to-text) is now gated behind Copilot Pro although it runs fully on-device – please re-enable the local backend without entitlement**
> 
> ### Summary
> 
> Since **VS Code 1.133.0**, the built-in dictation (speech-to-text) feature is locked behind a **paid Copilot plan**, even though the transcription itself runs **entirely on-device** (local ASR model via Foundry Local / "Nemotron", backend `nemo`). Users with a GitHub **Free** plan – or with **BYOK / no Copilot entitlement at all** – silently lost a feature that worked fine in 1.132.0 and earlier. Please re-enable dictation for the **local backend** without requiring a Copilot entitlement.
> 
> ### The core problem: a purely local feature was made paid
> 
> The new gate in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/chatSpeechToTextService.ts` is:
> 
> ```ts
> type DictationBackend = 'nemo' | 'mai';
> 
> export function isDictationEntitled(entitlement: ChatEntitlement, isInternal: boolean, usesMai: boolean): boolean {
>     return isProUser(entitlement) && (!usesMai || entitlement !== ChatEntitlement.Enterprise || isInternal);
> }
> ```
> 
> - The `nemo` backend transcribes via `ILocalTranscriptionService` – **audio never leaves the machine**, no Copilot API call, no cloud cost, no Microsoft infrastructure involved.
> - The gate blocks **both** backends, including the local one. There is no way for a Free/BYOK user to opt into local-only dictation; the check is hard-coded (`_isEntitledForBackend` is called in `isConfigured`, `_start` and `_isCurrentStart`).
> - A purely on-device accessibility feature has no visible connection to a GitHub Copilot subscription – the link is not discoverable, not documented in the settings, and impossible to explain to end users.
> 
> ### Why this should be reverted (or at least scoped to the cloud backend)
> 
> **1. It is a silent regression.**
> Dictation (including the local model) worked in 1.132.0 and earlier. 1.133.0 silently introduced the gate – the unit test is literally named *"requires a paid plan and restricts MAI for external Enterprise users"* and asserts `freeLocal: false`. Users who relied on this feature lost it overnight, with no announcement, no migration path, and no setting.
> 
> **2. It gates an accessibility feature behind a subscription.**
> Speech-to-text is a first-class accessibility feature (it is grouped with the Voice Mode/agentsVoice workbench contributions). Paywalling an accessibility feature is a poor experience and can be a legal problem in regions with accessibility legislation – especially since the feature does not consume any cloud resources in local mode.
> 
> **3. It breaks enterprise / air-gapped / BYOK setups.**
> Many organizations run VS Code with BYOK keys or fully air-gapped, with **no** Copilot entitlement at all. Dictation was previously usable without GitHub sign-in; those users now lose it. Note that the same gate even blocks **external Enterprise** users from the cloud (`mai`) backend – so the feature becomes a license-management headache instead of a productivity/accessibility tool.
> 
> **4. It pushes users to third-party extensions.**
> Because the built-in feature is gated, users install third-party speech extensions instead (several exist and work well). That is a worse, less integrated experience and fragments the ecosystem – the opposite of what a core workbench feature should achieve. Re-enabling local dictation would keep users on the supported, integrated path.
> 
> **5. The graceful-degradation pattern already exists.**
> The LLM cleanup step (`copilot-utility-small`) already falls back to the raw transcript when no utility model is available. The same pattern is the correct one for entitlement: gate only what actually uses Copilot/cloud resources, fall back gracefully for everything else. The `!usesMai ||` branch in `isDictationEntitled` shows the local exemption is trivial to implement.
> 
> ### Suggested change
> 
> ```ts
> // Only the cloud backend should require entitlement:
> return usesMai ? isProUser(entitlement) && (entitlement !== ChatEntitlement.Enterprise || isInternal) : true;
> ```
> 
> Or, minimal variant: keep `isDictationEntitled` as-is but return `true` for the `nemo` backend in `_isEntitledForBackend`.
> 
> ### Evidence
> 
> - Backends: `type DictationBackend = 'nemo' | 'mai'`; `_getBackend()` resolves `"nemo"` for the local path.
> - Regression: 1.132.0 did not import `IChatEntitlementService` at all; 1.133.0 added the import, `onDidChangeEntitlement` handling and the gate.
> - Test asserting the intent: `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatSpeechToTextService.test.ts` → *"requires a paid plan and restricts MAI for external Enterprise users"* (`freeLocal: false`).
> - Local transcription is handled by `ILocalTranscriptionService` (Foundry Local model, downloaded to the user's machine).
> 
> ### Environment
> 
> - VS Code 1.133.0 stable (also reproduced in 1.134.0 insiders)
> - Windows 11, GitHub account with Free plan (no paid Copilot), BYOK usage
> - Works fine with local model after removing the gate; the feature itself is fully functional on-device
>  

 _Originally posted by @Knubbel in [#329418](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329418#issuecomment-5284410751)_

title: Render a window shadow on the floating chat input window
body:
## Description

The Omni chat input hosts its content in a frameless, transparent auxiliary window sized tightly to the input. With no chrome and no shadow, it doesn't read as a separate window and gets mistaken for an inline input box.

Since the window bounds hug the surface, a `box-shadow` alone would be clipped at the window edge. The fix reserves a transparent gutter around the surface and grows the window bounds by that gutter, so the shadow renders into the transparent band while the input keeps its exact content size.

- **`media/chatInputWindow.css`** — introduce `--omni-window-shadow-size: 16px`, drive the surface `margin` / `height` calc from it (replacing the 1px stroke), and add `box-shadow: 0 3px 10px 0 var(--vscode-widget-shadow, …)` (matching the shadow token used by suggest/action widgets).
- **`chatInputWindowService.ts`** — add `CHAT_INPUT_WINDOW_SHADOW_SIZE = 16` (kept in sync with the CSS var); `fitWindowToInput` and `_defaultBounds` now pad width/height by `2 * shadow` so the surface size is preserved and the shadow isn't clipped.

Pending-approval panel sizing and action-widget anchoring measure relative `getBoundingClientRect()`s, so the inset gutter is transparent to them.

- Fixes #331179

title: Show send-button spinner immediately on Omni chat submit
body:
Submitting from the Omni chat input felt unresponsive after pressing Enter. The pending indicator appeared late, rendered alongside the Agent-mode send button instead of replacing it, and routing could spend tens of seconds scoring the full session catalog before the countdown began.

## Description

- Set the custom-submit pending state at the start of `ChatWidget.acceptInput`, before dictation shutdown, view-model readiness, editor saving, and routing.
- Refresh the execute toolbar synchronously when pending state changes so the spinner does not wait for a debounced menu update.
- Drive the spinner from `chatInputSubmitPending` for its full lifetime: routing, destination countdown, and dispatch.
- Hide and disable both Ask- and Agent-mode send actions while submission is pending, so the spinner replaces the send button rather than appearing beside it.
- Restore the send action when submission is rejected, cancelled, aborted, or fails.
- Bound routing work before the countdown. Previously, 167 candidates were sent through one model request to select 12 candidates, followed by a second model request for final routing. Local logs measured 22.9 seconds in this stage. The initial shortlist now uses the existing synchronous heuristic, leaving one semantic model request with at most 12 candidates.

The intentional five-second destination countdown remains unchanged so users can review or change the selected target before dispatch.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- 39 focused chat submit and session-routing tests
- Regression coverage verifies that, in Agent mode, the pending spinner is visible while the send action is hidden.

title: Flatten markdown headings in omni bar routing badge preview
body:
The omni bar's completed-session badge previews the first line of a session's response as markdown. When that line is a heading (`# Current session activity`), it rendered as a full-size `<h1>`, reading like a title rather than a snippet, with no cue that more content follows.

## Changes
- **Flatten block markdown** — `responsePreview` strips leading heading (`#`), blockquote (`>`), and list (`-`/`*`/`+`) markers so the previewed line renders inline. Inline markdown (e.g. links) is preserved.
- **Indicate continuation** — `responsePreview` detects whether the response extends past the previewed line; `renderCompletedResponse` appends `…` when it does.

Result: `# Current session activity\n\nThree sessions are running.` now renders as `Completed session activity: Current session activity…` instead of an oversized heading.

## How to test
- Route a request to a session whose response begins with a markdown heading and spans multiple lines; confirm the badge shows inline text with a trailing ellipsis and no `<h1>`.
- Single-line responses render unchanged (no ellipsis, links intact).

title: terminal: fix stale-state ETX
body:
# src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts:
Only send ^C before executing a command when the prompt truly contains user input. Detection now uses prefix + suffix length (which exclude ghost text and PSReadLine predictions) instead of the full input value, and treats the state as stale when the cursor index is -1 (command line came from a shell integration report rather than observed keystrokes) or when the value is only a continuation prompt (e.g. PowerShell "> ") and should be ignored.

This is the key modification that fixes #316222.

# src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/browser/sessionChangesEditor.ts:
During the first full REH server build (`vscode-reh-win32-x64`, i.e. the `compile-build-with-mangling` task), the build failed at the **mangling step**. The mangler rewrites private members to short names before packaging, and it aborts on visibility violations. 

Add the `protected` modifier to the `updateChecked` and `getTooltip` overrides in ChangesetReviewActionViewItem so their visibility matches the overridden members in the base class.

This fix is required because I need to test this patch on the real Remote-SSH server. The OSS-TestResolver cannot reproduce the ^C issue.

# src/vs/workbench/services/extensions/common/extensionPoints.json:
This file was **not edited by hand**. It appeared in the working tree after a compile step that includes the extension-point scan, and it will reappear automatically whenever that scan runs.

Inside `build/lib/compilation.ts`, the compile pipeline scans every source file for `ExtensionsRegistry.registerExtensionPoint(...)` call sites, parses the `extensionPoint: '...'` name out of each registration with the TypeScript compiler API, sorts all collected names, and rewrites `src/vs/workbench/services/extensions/common/extensionPoints.json`.
